editorNote: A busy week for getting somewhere: two probes slingshot toward Mars, a Starship test is poised to try a double catch, and astronomers keep turning up faint, dark things at the Milky Way's edge and beyond. Several results are early, and the starless-galaxy candidate in particular awaits follow-up.

stories.headline: ESCAPADE's twin spacecraft complete powered Earth flybys and head for Mars
stories.summary: Both NASA ESCAPADE probes used Earth's gravity plus a roughly nine-minute engine burn at closest approach, planned for Nov. 7 and Nov. 9, to speed toward Mars. Each burn was planned to add more than 1,000 mph.
stories.whyItMatters: NASA calls it the first time the agency has used a powered Earth flyby to send a spacecraft to Mars; the pair are due to arrive in September 2027 to fly in formation there.

sourceLinks.title: NASA's Twin ESCAPADE Spacecraft to Slingshot Past Earth on Way to Mars

stories.headline: Rubin Observatory's early data reveals a new ultra-faint Milky Way satellite and a hidden star cluster
stories.summary: Aquarius IV, an ultra-faint satellite galaxy, and Rubin-GC1, a star cluster behind the dusty far side of the Milky Way, both turned up in preview data taken between April 2025 and January 2026, covering about 15% of the survey footprint.
stories.whyItMatters: About 65 Milky Way satellites are known; the finds are a preview of what the 10-year survey, begun in June, may add.

sourceLinks.title: University of Washington: Rubin Observatory Milky Way satellites

stories.headline: A giant hydrogen cloud with no visible stars may be a rotating 'dark' galaxy
stories.summary: Swinburne University astronomers, comparing Arecibo and FAST radio surveys, found AGC 322753: about 2 billion solar masses of hydrogen, at least 40 times its stellar mass, with a double-peaked signal that may mean rotation.
stories.whyItMatters: Models say dark galaxies shouldn't rotate, but the team cautions it may hold faint stars or be tidal debris; Very Large Array follow-up is planned.

sourceLinks.title: Scientists May Have Discovered a Massive Starless Galaxy (syndicated Wired report)

stories.headline: SpaceX targets Nov. 13 for Starship Flight 15, aiming to catch both booster and ship
stories.summary: SpaceX released Flight 15 details on Nov. 7: the Super Heavy booster is to be caught minutes after liftoff and the ship about 22.5 hours later, after roughly 14 orbits, pending regulatory approval.
stories.whyItMatters: The flight would be the first attempt to catch both stages; as of publication it has not flown and the date is a target.

sourceLinks.title: SpaceX plans to catch both Starship stages on Flight 15
